rule: D-025 clarity re-voice, judged on D-022 as ruled for this pass by D-026, and the voice/takes.clarity.<lang>.json notes
method: Local only, no connector transcription. Transcripts: whisper.cpp whisper-cli ggml-small, greedy, no prompt, script not given: -l <lang>; Hindi takes also -l en (transcript_latin_pass, shows whether the English words were heard); every take also -l auto (language id). Doubtful words: each speech segment cut (+-0.08 s) and transcribed alone with ggml-small, plus ggml-base as a second model (ggml-large-v3 is not in ~/.whisper-models, so it was not used). Measures: copies of the D-022 round-3 meas.py and seg.py, unchanged: speech frames are 20 ms RMS within 35 dB of the take's loudest frame (floor -55 dBFS); voiced_ratio is the share of speech frames with normalised autocorrelation (8 kHz, 70-450 Hz lags) of 0.6 or more; segments split at gaps of 150 ms or more. D-022 test on voice-wanted lines: whole take and every segment of 0.5 s or more that carries script words at 0.6 or more, applied as ruled by D-026: retake only real faults (wrong or missing words, whispered or breathy words, glitches, wrong language); words voiced at speaking level whose segment falls under 0.6 only on consonant or breath tails are accepted and go on the ear list. Nobody listened.
edit_pick: The edit reads voice/manifest.jsonl and voice/review.json, not this file. The runner wrote each clarity row's manifest take as the line's next take (not renumbered here); a matching row (verdict ok, model eleven_v4, same take) was appended to review.json, so build_timeline.py cuts in the .c1 take (checked with a replica of pick_take).
